chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Abu Jamilah, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who made a vow to Allah but did not specify anything, he said: 'He fasts for six days.'

key_terms.نَذْرًا: A vow or promise made to God to perform an act of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a vow to Allah where the specific act was not mentioned?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a default expiation for a general vow (*nadhr*) where the specific act was not designated, ruling that the vow-maker must fast for six days. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of providing a manageable, specific obligation to fulfill the intent of the vow when the details are ambiguous, ensuring the vow is discharged without undue hardship.
